announcements.title: ABBA v0.11.0 Released
announcements.content:
Welcome to ABBA 0.11.0!

New features and improvements

Standard Export: Share your projects as standardized .zip files with resampled data and metadata.

QuickNII Integration: Import and export QuickNII projects.

Methods Generator: Use an automatically generated prompt to get publication-ready methods with DOIs and registration details.

Brightfield images: Added support for white background, eliminating black edge artifacts during registration.

Plus: New light/dark themes, improved UI with icons, drag-and-drop support, and much more!

announcements.title: ABBA v0.25.0 Released
announcements.content:
ABBA 0.25.0 has been released.

No more conda, and an AI assistant that can drive ABBA

The update site has moved: ABBA is now published on the UNIGE-Biochem update site, not PTBIOP. Enable it in Help > Update... > Manage update sites to keep receiving ABBA updates. ABBA needs Java 21, which an up-to-date Fiji has.

Nothing else to install: DeepSlice, Elastix and BrainGlobe atlases set themselves up the first time you use them. No conda, no elastix executable, no paths to set.

With an AI assistant (experimental): one click in VS Code, or one line in Claude or Codex, and an assistant registers your slices in ABBA's window, where you can take over at any time. See the installation page, which also describes the new ABBA installer.

Easier corrections: adjust several slices in one Manual Affine window, and undo registration edits, rotations and flips.

Plus: export slices opened from files to a new QuPath project, a name filter in the slices table, demo slices from Zenodo, clearer error messages, and a rewritten documentation.

The first DeepSlice or Elastix registration downloads its environment, which takes a few minutes. ABBA stands on the work of many people: thank you to all of them.
